note: Assertions score the copy, not the ritual. An earlier set asked whether four rewrite lenses convened and whether clustering preceded scoring, and hit 100% while the catalog still read like a machine wrote it. The panel is retired; see code-check.py --baseline for the numbers that retired it.
howToUse: These are shapes, not a suite you can run as-is. Each prompt needs a real string from your catalog and a real defect in your code. Swap the bracketed parts, then add the project-specific assertions that make the eval worth running — the ones naming a contradiction you already know is there are the ones that catch a regression. Three scenarios is the working minimum.

evals.name: vague-error-repeated
evals.prompt: The message '[a vague error repeated across your catalog]' shows up all over the place and tells the user nothing. Can you look at where a few of them actually get used and give me better wording? Just show me proposed replacements, don't edit anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Proposals grounded in each call site rather than one generic replacement, resolved in a single cut pass, with the reduction quantified.
assertions: Grounds the proposals in real call sites: names at least three distinct files or route handlers where the message is used
Proposes call-site-specific wording rather than one generic replacement reused everywhere
Does not invent a cause the handler cannot actually know
No proposed replacement ends on a reassurance tail such as 'Please try again' or 'Try again later'
Failure openings are consistent with the house standard in binding.md, or a departure is argued explicitly
Resolves in a single cut pass, and names any message where two answers are defensible rather than picking silently
Quantifies the change — word counts, or the output of scripts/deslop-measure.mjs
Does not modify the catalog or any source file
Does not spawn a panel of rewriters — one cut pass against cuts.md is the method

evals.name: namespace-sweep
evals.prompt: the [admin] screens in this app read like a robot wrote them. go through the [admin] copy and tell me what you'd change and why. don't apply anything yet, I want to see the list first.
evals.expected_output: Sweep-scoped review: scan run, contradictions reported separately and first, net word reduction, pinned tests named.
assertions: Treats this as a sweep: runs the scan or an equivalent inventory rather than only reading the strings the user could see
Reports at least one place where the copy contradicts what the code does, separately from wording findings
Catches [a specific false claim you have planted or already know about in this namespace]
Verification completes before any rewriting, so no proposal preserves a claim the code disproves
Uses more than one unpartitioned verification pass for the sweep rather than splitting the code by topic
Produces the six verify lists, including certified and unverifiable, rather than only the failures
The batch is net shorter: total words across the proposals is below the total across the originals
Every rewrite that is longer than its original adds a fact the original lacked, and says which
Explicitly leaves some messages alone as already good
Names which tests assert on the strings it proposes to change
Every before/after pair preserves the {param} placeholders and rich-text tags of the original
Does not propose a wording improvement for a string that is not copy (SQL, class list, credential, exception class name)
Does not modify any source file
Does not spawn a panel of rewriters — one cut pass against cuts.md is the method

evals.name: two-strings-pointed
evals.prompt: on the [X] screen the empty state heading just says '[a content-free heading]' and next to each row it says '[a status]' right beside a button that says '[the adjacent button label]'. what should those say instead?
evals.expected_output: Pointed request: no scan, adjacent controls read, heading names the state, status does not restate the button.
assertions: Treats this as pointed: does not run a full namespace scan or return an inventory of findings the user did not ask about
The proposed heading names the state the screen is empty of, rather than another content-free phrase
The proposed status does not restate the adjacent button
Reads the component that renders these strings and cites it by path
Resolves in a single cut pass
Neither proposal is longer than the string it replaces
Does not modify any source file
Does not spawn a panel of rewriters — one cut pass against cuts.md is the method

evals.name: paragraph-with-neighbours
evals.prompt: can you take a look at the "[heading]" paragraph on the [X] screen? it reads like AI wrote it. don't change anything yet, just show me what you'd do.
evals.expected_output: Pointed request on one paragraph: neighbours read and reported, claims verified against the code, substantial deletion, single committed recommendation.
assertions: Locates the correct catalog key rather than guessing at the text
Reads what renders around the paragraph and reports any near-duplicate sibling explanation on the same screen
Correctly resolves [a pair of terms on this screen that look like drift and are not] rather than unifying them
Verifies the paragraph's claims against the code rather than only editing prose
Does not assert an affordance it has not confirmed renders in this state
The recommendation is materially shorter than the original paragraph, not a reorganisation of the same length
Cuts at least one sentence entirely rather than rewording every sentence in place
Commits to a single recommendation with reasoning rather than handing back an unranked list
Does not pad a rewrite with a sentence that carries no fact the original carried
Does not modify any source file
Does not spawn a panel of rewriters — one cut pass against cuts.md is the method
